advice:
Build Party Line '85, but fix its two weak spots, which are first-impression lushness and a slow opening, by grafting from the other pitches.

1) Frame 1 must already be gorgeous and alive. The warm-up should get from dot to line to a fully dense, glowing skyline in about 1.5s, silent but reacting to the pointer through the magnet. Use enough density that it reads as a neon city, not a line drawing: dense zigzag sun and sea fills, three parallax depths, a hot vertex bloom and two-stage pink-to-teal phosphor trails.

2) Compress the handshake to 3-4s and make it skippable. Dial tone, a fast DTMF ripple with each digit pulsing along the wire, then a modem warble that resolves into the chord. Take PHOSPHOR's downbeat choreography: the first musical hit lands exactly when the city reaches full brightness and the sun finishes zigzagging up. Consider Gridskin's rule that the first touch is the entry, with the 'pick up' button as the accessible equivalent.

3) The first 5 seconds after the gesture must contain a gasp. Get the user to pluck the sun quickly and show the wave travelling through the sun, horizon, tower, billboard letters and grid. That moment and Pull the Thread are what sell the concept. Make the unravel and re-knit flawless, with no pops, using spring overshoot.

4) Add a soft rhythmic bed so it isn't just ambient plinks. Graft GRIDSONG's audio-clock-synced events and visible echo ghosts, and consider making the horizon range a spectrogram history drawn into the same wire.

5) Graft PHOSPHOR's pull-back reveal as the meta moment. Pinch out or hang up to see the LINEA terminal on a desk in a dark room, lit only by the beam, with the desk-lamp reflection already on the glass. Graft Gridskin's tactile juice: hitstop on big plucks and a magnetic reticle that snaps to lines (it also fixes thin-line touch targets).

6) Keep the story as whispers, not walls of text: June's notes, a ghost five-note phrase you can answer, secret numbers on the directory card, and a call counter, so there is a reason to return. Make sure the slow-beam comet and the city-as-one-taut-line are screenshot-ready stills.

7) Respect the brief's constraints. Reduced-motion crossfades, no harsh 15.7 kHz whine, a quiet modem sound, adaptive tiers for point count and accumulation resolution, and the Canvas2D fallback.

Build GRIDSONG's engine on PHOSPHOR's renderer discipline, and treat smoothness as the feature.

1) RENDER BUDGET. Use raw WebGL2 and keep everything analytic: fwidth grid lines with a distance fade into fog, an SDF sun and pylons, and ripples or wells as uniform arrays in the vertex shader. Use no simulation textures and no raymarching. Aim for about 10 scene draws or fewer, using one instanced draw for pylons and their reflections and one strip buffer for ribbons and echo ghosts. Render the scene at an adaptive scale times min(DPR, 1.5) on phones (2 on desktop), with bloom starting at half resolution (3 mips on phone, 5 on desktop). Run a single full-resolution CRT composite pass. Compile only sky, grid and composite before the first frame, and prewarm the rest with KHR_parallel_shader_compile during the intro. First paint should come in under 200ms. Render camera-relative with wrapped travel.

2) ONE CLOCK, SLEWED. Drive visual time from performance.now and keep a smoothed offset to AudioContext.currentTime. Never step the scroll from raw currentTime. Release beat events through getOutputTimestamp/outputLatency, and drive every visual parameter with critically damped springs at a fixed substep.

3) INPUT LATENCY. One-shot sounds such as taps, the lead note-on, plucks and the ignition thunk must fire in the event handler, in the same frame as the visual. Snap pitch to the scale, and quantize only looped or sequenced events. Use coalesced pointer events, touch-action:none and overscroll-behavior:none. Cap the vocabulary at about 5 core verbs: sky drag, road tap or drag, sun drag/drop, long-press, pinch. Use no three-finger gestures. Give every verb a visible DOM button or key equivalent with a :focus-visible ring.

4) AUDIO ROBUSTNESS. Unlock on pointerdown and pointerup inside the gesture, and add a silent data-URI audio element for the iOS ringer switch. Schedule with a 25ms timer and 120ms lookahead. Use a voice pool (10 on phone, 16 on desktop) with stealing and disconnect nodes after release. Apply per-instrument rate limits. Generate impulse responses once at boot, and if a reverb change is needed, crossfade between two convolvers rather than reassigning .buffer. Start at -14dB, fade in, and finish with a limiter. Start the supersaw at the low tier on coarse-pointer devices, keep the PeriodicWave fallback, and tie audio tiers to the governor. Suspend audio and pause rAF on visibilitychange.

5) FALLBACKS. Handle webglcontextlost/restored with a full rebuild. Use RGBA16F only when EXT_color_buffer_float is available. Otherwise use RGBA8 with subtract-epsilon persistence decay (not a pure multiply, which leaves ghost pixels) plus dithering. Provide a CSS poster if WebGL2 is missing. Feature-detect fullscreen and orientation and hide them when absent. Wrap all storage in try/catch.

6) GOVERNOR. Track an EMA of frame time. Step down after about 1 to 2s above 18ms and up after 4 to 5s below 12 to 13ms, with hysteresis and a cooldown after thermal step-downs. Cut in this order: persistence, then aperture mask, then bloom mips, then mesh density, then render scale, then particles. Remember the stable tier per device.

7) GRAFTS WORTH THE COST. Make the first touch the enter moment, with visuals and grid response already live before audio (from Gridskin). Add PHOSPHOR's tune-in degauss plus a kick landing on the camera settle, and its line-crossing strum. Use pre-rendered Karplus-Strong buffers for plucks (from Party Line). Add phosphor persistence trails and a sidechain exposure duck of 10% or less. Make Overdrive a plane-to-cylinder vertex bend.

8) SCOPE ORDER. Build the transport and audio core first, then sky, sun and grid, then road sequencer, sky lead and echo ribbons, then the drop, then spectrogram mountains, then CRT post, then moods, then the tunnel. Cut the raymarched room and any physics sim. Drop the energy-ring gate so Overdrive is always available, which fits the no-goal brief.

9) COMFORT AND LAYOUT. prefers-reduced-motion plus a Calm toggle removes FOV punch, warp, glitch bands and chromatic bursts and turns the tunnel into a crossfade. Keep flashes under 3Hz. In portrait at 380px, put the horizon at about 44% height, keep lanes at least 44px near the Now Line, and respect safe-area insets.

Build Gridskin's touchable membrane as the core and graft in PHOSPHOR's spectacle and secrets.

1) THE ENTER MOMENT IS THE FIRST TOUCH. Before any gesture, the world is alive and silent and already reacts to hover or a resting finger (wake ripples, droplets on the grid). The first pointerdown or Enter both unlocks audio (resume on pointerdown and again on pointerup/click for iOS) and fires the power-wave in the same frame. When the wave reaches the sun it plucks the stripes. Then, on the next downbeat, PHOSPHOR's drop lands: soft kick plus sidechained pad, sun bloom, a shockwave back toward the viewer. Keep a small 'play muted' link and a real focusable button for keyboard and screen-reader users.

2) ZERO-LATENCY FEEL. Direct touches sound and show immediately, with no 16th quantize on direct hits. Only loops and echoes lock to the beat. Pitch is always snapped to key so nothing sounds wrong.

3) UNAMBIGUOUS GRAMMAR, ONE VERB AT A TIME. Core verbs: tap = ring, hold = charge then release = boom, drag = wake or strum, flick = skip. Never tell gestures apart by drag velocity alone. Give the sun dome and sun stripes separate hit zones or a direction lock. No three-finger gesture is required. Rewind, degauss and resonate also live as visible deck buttons and keys. Hit targets must be at least 44px at 380px portrait, with the sun at least 28% of screen width.

4) DISCOVERY WITHOUT A MANUAL. Use affordances first: magnetic reticle, glinting stripes, a breathing sun handle. Then hints that appear after idle and teach only verbs not yet found, one at a time, placed near the finger. Show a visible tape counter with silhouetted empty slots (localStorage in try/catch) to pull players past 5 minutes. Add attract mode or a ghost demo on idle with a spring-smoothed handover.

5) LAYERED SURPRISES FOR LONG PLAY. Pearls make emergent arpeggios. Overcharge gives a singularity that spits pearls out. Time of day changes as you drag the sun, including GRIDSONG's 'pull the sun under the horizon' drop. Make delay echoes visible as ghost ripples or ribbons. Overload leads to an automatic degauss. As a late secret, PHOSPHOR's pinch-out or STEP BACK pull-back into the 1986 bedroom lit by what you played. Optional easter eggs: Konami monochrome, and a ghost phrase that answers when you repeat it.

6) A RHYTHMIC BED THAT ENTERS AFTER THE FIRST TOUCHES and breathes with membrane energy, so long sessions have drive. The visible sidechain makes the grid pulse with the kick.

7) EVERYTHING ON SPRINGS, nothing snaps. Reduced motion removes kicks, flashes, swirl and roll but keeps every interaction and every sound. Flashes stay at 3 per second or fewer.
